''Potamogeton fluitans'' }} '''''Potamogeton nodosus''''' is a species of [[aquatic plant]] known by the common names '''longleaf pondweed'''{{PLANTS|id=PONO2|taxon=Potamogeton nodosus|accessdate=13 October 2015}} and '''Loddon pondweed'''.{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }} It is native to Eurasia and the Americas, where it is widespread and can be found in water bodies such as ponds, lakes, ditches, and streams. This is a perennial herb producing a thin, branching stem easily exceeding a meter in maximum length. The submerged leaves are linear to widely lance-shaped and up to {{convert|15|x|4|cm|in}} in length and width, respectively, while the floating leaves achieve shorter maximum lengths and are ovate or elliptic.{{cite web|first1=C. Barre|last1=Hellquist|first2=Robert F.|last2=Thorne|last3=Haynes|first3=Robert R.|url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=39595|publisher=Regents of the University of California|website=Jepson eFlora|title=''Potamogeton nodosus'' Long-Leaved Pondweed|year=2012|editor=Jepson Flora Project|access-date=25 November 2023}} Both floating leaves and submerged leaves are borne on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]], a distinguishing characteristic.
